item.title: Uwajima Castle: A Small Original Keep — Guide
item.description: Uwajima Castle, in the southern port city of Uwajima, is one of Japan’s twelve castles to retain its original Edo-period wooden keep. Small and elegant rather than grand, its three-storey white tower crowns a wooded hill in the middle of the city, reached by a climb through stone walls and old gates among the trees. Built by the Date clan who ruled the domain, it survived the centuries intact and offers a genuine taste of a modest samurai-era castle, with views over Uwajima and its bay from the top.
